title: Quarterly systems map: hosted API & model catalog alignment across dual-track execution
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Objective: produce a single, actionable quarterly roadmap artifact that ties Hosted API route commitments to model-catalog slots, defines commit windows, and prescribes contingency paths for capacity or quality regressions.

Scope: cross-team alignment doc + milestone map for the quarter covering: model onboarding cadence, endpoint tiering decisions, canary windows, rollback/backstop policies, telemetry and eval gates, and customer migration guidance. Includes a minimal decision protocol for pruning low-usage endpoints and an emergency surge plan.

Why now: demand signal from Q1 showed unpredictable spikes across two hosted endpoints; we need a coordinated policy that reduces operational surprises while enabling rapid model swaps. This ticket consolidates PM/Eng/Design inputs into a roadmap that can be published to stakeholders and used by Solutions/CS for customer comms.

Deliverables:
- Quarter map PDF + one-pager for execs (Deliverable A)
- Milestone timeline (week-by-week) with owners (Deliverable B)
- Canary and rollback checklist (Deliverable C)
- Telemetry dashboard spec (Grafana + cost breakout) and alert thresholds (Deliverable D)
- Model slot prioritization spreadsheet + usage threshold rules (Deliverable E)

Success metrics:
- 90% of planned endpoint/model swaps have a canary pass within the commitment window
- <5 customer-visible incidents due to model rotation in quarter
- Cost per 1k tokens for top-10 endpoints reduced by >=6% through batching/quantization recommendations

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We will limit the initial model lineup for the quarter to the top 6 slots to reduce roll complexity; this slows discovery for fringe models but reduces operational blast radius.
- Canary windows default to 14 days; this increases lead time but improves signal quality.
- Telemetry depends on an ENG task to instrument per-route token breakdown (ENG-33211 listed below).

Open questions:
- Should Dedicated customers get a different canary cadence? (proposal: yes, 7-day canaries by request)
- How aggressive should automatic downgrade policies be for quality regressions? (options: auto-fallback to previous model vs. throttle routing to lower tier)

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Artifact set (A-E) uploaded to Confluence and linked from this ticket
- Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime Eng, Console PM, and Solutions by the end of planning cycle
- GitHub PRs for telemetry dashboard + cost sheet exist and are reviewed

Notes on cross-team coordination:
- Weekly syncs scheduled with Runtime (Wed 10am), Console (Thu 3pm), and Customer Success (Fri 9am) during the planning window.
- Design to provide a one-slide executive summary and a short customer-facing FAQ.
